transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Lately I’ve been overwhelmed by guilt about letting everyone down at home and at work, even when people tell me it’s not that bad. It just feels like I'm failing everyone, and I can't seem to shake this heavy feeling.
Have you had one or more similar episodes of depression before, or is this the first time you’ve ever felt this way?

This isn't the first time, actually. I've had these cycles of sinking into long, low, drained stretches—alternating with periods of feeling overly revved up—on and off for at least a few years, though they've gotten much more noticeable recently. This current low stretch has been dragging on for about five months now.
During this current low period, have you been unable to work, care for yourself, or do your usual daily activities because of how severe the depression is?

Yes, it has really taken a toll. At work, I've been missing deadlines and forgetting meetings, so my team has had to quietly pick up my slack. Even simple things like getting ready or loading the dishwasher feel completely exhausting, and I keep backing out of plans with my family and friends because I just can't bring myself to go.
During this depressive episode, have you been so slowed down or agitated that it is hard to do basic things like shower, dress, eat, or concentrate enough to get through the day?

Yes, absolutely. My body feels like it's moving through molasses, and even basic tasks like getting ready or loading the dishwasher exhaust me completely. I've also been skipping meals because I have no appetite, and my mind often blanks out, making it hard to follow conversations or even decide what to cook.
During this current depression, have you been unable to do basic self-care or daily tasks most days because of the depression, such as bathing, dressing, eating, or getting through work?

Yes, most days it feels almost impossible to keep up. I've been skipping meals because I just don't have an appetite, and simple things like getting dressed or loading the dishwasher completely drain me. At work, it's gotten to the point where I'm missing deadlines and my team has to quietly pick up my slack.
During this current depressive episode, have you been unable to do basic self-care or daily tasks most days because of the depression, such as bathing, dressing, eating, or getting through work?

Yes, managing daily life and work has become incredibly difficult and overwhelming. I'm so exhausted that getting ready or loading the dishwasher takes everything I have, and I often skip meals or freeze up over simple decisions like what to cook. At work, I've been missing deadlines and forgetting meetings, forcing my team to quietly pick up my slack.
During this depression, have you had thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself, and I don't feel like life isn't worth living. Even though I feel incredibly guilty and overwhelmed, those kinds of thoughts haven't crossed my mind.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, and were more talkative, confident, or impulsive than usual?

Yes, right before this low stretch, I had a few weeks after a big work launch where I felt incredibly upbeat but also touchy, sleeping only four hours a night and waking up completely wired. I felt so confident that I took on way too many projects at once, and my coworkers even joked that I was talking too fast. These cycles of feeling revved up and then crashing have actually been happening on and off for a few years.

Have you ever had a period that lasted at least 4 days where you felt unusually high, irritable, or energized and needed much less sleep, but it did not cause major problems like hospitalization or severe impairment?

Yes, I had exactly that kind of period for several weeks after a successful program launch at work, where I felt unusually upbeat but also touchy and irritable. I had a massive surge of energy, taking on tons of new projects and needing only about four hours of sleep a night while still waking up completely wired. It didn't lead to anything like hospitalization, but it was highly noticeable to my family and coworkers.
During those high-energy periods, did you ever become so impaired that you needed hospitalization, or have symptoms like psychosis, dangerous behavior, or complete inability to function?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized, experienced psychosis, or been unable to function during those times. I was actually highly active and productive, successfully launching a new program at work, though my impulsivity and overcommitting did cause some strain and annoyance for my family and coworkers.
Have you ever had a period of at least 7 days when your mood was so elevated or irritable that it caused major problems at work, at home, or required hospitalization, or involved psychosis?

Yes, those high-energy periods did last for several weeks, which is well over seven days. But they never led to hospitalization, psychosis, or total dysfunction; in fact, I felt highly productive and successful at work during those times. The real problems and impairment only set in afterward, when I crashed into this current low state.
During this current low period, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or do you mostly just feel sad, guilty, and exhausted?

It is actually both. I’ve completely lost interest in things I used to love, like my Saturday hikes and art classes, which I keep canceling because they just feel flat and pointless now. At the same time, I wake up every day with a heavy, gray feeling in my chest, constantly consumed by guilt about letting everyone down and feeling completely exhausted all day.
During your high-energy periods, did you ever have symptoms severe enough to cause major impairment, psychosis, or need hospitalization, or were they noticeable but not that severe?

They were definitely noticeable to others, with coworkers joking about me talking too fast and a colleague saying I didn't seem like myself because I was overcommitting to so many projects. However, they were never severe enough to cause psychosis, require hospitalization, or cause any real destruction during the high phase itself.
During your high-energy periods, did you ever have symptoms severe enough to cause major problems at work, at home, or to require hospitalization, or were they noticeable but not that severe?

They were definitely noticeable to others, but they weren't severe enough to cause major disasters or require hospitalization. People at work noticed I was talking very fast and overcommitting to projects, and at home I was a bit touchy and snapped at my daughter, but it felt more like a period of intense productivity and being "revved up" rather than a severe crisis.

During those high-energy periods, did your symptoms ever become severe enough that you had major trouble functioning at work or at home, or were they more like a noticeable but manageable boost in energy and confidence?

It was definitely more of a noticeable, intense boost in energy and confidence where I felt on top of the world and took on way too many projects. I didn't have trouble functioning then, even though I was a bit irritable and overcommitted. The real struggle with missing deadlines and withdrawing from everyone only started once I hit this low, depressed phase.
Has this current depressed period lasted at least 2 weeks, or has it been mostly a few days at a time?

Yes, it has lasted much longer than two weeks. This current low stretch has actually been dragging on for about five months now, starting shortly after that busy, high-energy period I had around the time of the program rollout at work.
When you had those high-energy periods, did they ever cause major problems at work or at home, or were they more of a noticeable but manageable boost in energy and confidence?

It was definitely more of an intense, highly confident boost where I felt like I could handle absolutely anything on my own. While people noticed I was "not like myself" because I was talking too fast and overcommitting, it didn't cause any major crises at the time. The real problems, like missing deadlines and letting people down, only started once that energy faded and I crashed into this low phase.

During your high-energy periods, did you ever become so impaired that you needed hospitalization, had psychosis, or were unable to function at work or at home? Or were those periods noticeable but not severe enough to cause major impairment?

Those periods were definitely noticeable to others—my coworkers joked about me talking too fast and a colleague mentioned I didn't seem like myself—but they never led to hospitalization or psychosis. Instead of being unable to function, I actually felt like I was functioning on overdrive, taking on extra projects and overcommitting. In hindsight, it was a chaotic pace, but at the time I felt like I could do anything.

Before this current low period, did you have at least two full months with no depression and feeling back to your usual self, or have these low and high periods been happening with only brief breaks in between?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact timeline of the breaks between my high and low periods. I can't quite recall how long I felt completely back to normal in between them, as everything has felt a bit blurry lately.
When you had those high-energy periods, did they last at least 4 days, or were they usually shorter than that?
Yes, they definitely lasted much longer than four days. Typically, those high-energy periods would go on for several weeks at a time before they eventually tapered off and I started to crash.

Between your high-energy periods and this current depression, did you ever have at least 2 months when your mood and energy were back to your usual baseline, or were the ups and downs happening with only brief breaks in between?

I'm not entirely sure if there was a clear two-month stretch of feeling completely normal, as these phases have just been "on and off" over the last few years. This current low started pretty soon after my high-energy period ended, so the transition felt fairly quick this time around.

I'm really not sure about the exact duration of my normal periods or how long they typically last between these cycles. I haven't really tracked the timeline of my baseline moods in the past, so it's hard to say for sure.
